tool_description: System process monitoring and management. Lists processes sorted by CPU or RAM, finds resource hogs, identifies which process owns a port, watches specific processes for crashes, and handles termination with mandatory confirmation.

available_commands.description: List running processes sorted by cpu or ram
Find processes exceeding CPU (50%) or RAM (500MB) thresholds
Find which process is using a specific port
Find all processes matching a name
Propose killing a process — REQUIRES confirm_kill before executing
Execute the previously proposed kill after user confirmation
Cancel the pending kill without taking action
Watch a process and alert via thought buffer if it stops running
List all watched processes and their current status
Get CPU, RAM, disk, network stats and top 5 processes

tool_usage_guidance: Always use propose_kill first — never confirm_kill without a prior proposal
Protected processes cannot be killed: System, csrss, lsass, services, svchost, explorer, python.exe
Use watch_process to monitor critical processes like ollama — Anna will alert if they crash
Use find_by_port when something is blocking a port you need
system_overview gives the fastest snapshot of overall system state
Background context loop checks watched processes every 30 seconds
proactive_triggers: When user asks 'what is using the most CPU/RAM?'
When user asks 'what is on port X?'
When a watched process stops running
When user asks to kill or stop a process
When user asks for a system overview or resource usage

metadata.notes: Kill workflow requires two steps: propose_kill then confirm_kill. Protected system processes are blocked from termination.
